items.title: 8.3 Relation between macroscopic and microscopic events

blocks.text: Macroscopic events are the result of multiple simultaneous microscopic events, so understanding the microscopic events helps to explain and predict the observed macroscopic changes in an equilibrium system. When an equilibrium shifts, the microscopic events that explain the observed changes are the collisions and the formation of new bonds between particles; these collisions change the rates of the forward and reverse reactions, which are affected by the activation energy and by external factors, and together they appear as macroscopic changes visible to the naked eye.

blocks.prompt: The equilibrium is dynamic in nature. Explain this in terms of microscopic events.
blocks.explanation: At equilibrium nothing visible changes, but molecules of reactants are still colliding, breaking bonds and forming products, and molecules of products are still colliding and re-forming reactants. These opposite microscopic processes run at exactly equal rates, so their macroscopic result, the composition of the mixture, stays constant while the molecular activity never stops.

items: Macroscopic changes are the sum of many microscopic events; a shift of equilibrium is explained by collisions and bond formation that change the forward and reverse rates.
